entries.title: Flask & Extension Imports
entries.why: The dashboard is a Flask web application with multiple security and real-time extensions. Conditional imports allow graceful degradation if optional dependencies are missing.
entries.whatItDoes: Imports: Flask core, Flask-SocketIO (WebSockets), Flask-Talisman (CSP headers), Flask-Limiter (rate limiting), PyPDF2 (PDF parsing), Groq (AI), Kafka client, and ML components. Each optional import sets an *_AVAILABLE flag.

failureModes.behavior: SOCKETIO_AVAILABLE=False, 3D twin won't get real-time updates
No CSP headers, minor security reduction

entries.securityNotes: Optional security imports allow running in minimal mode during development

entries.title: Socket.IO Initialization
entries.why: Flask-SocketIO enables real-time bidirectional communication with the 3D digital twin. It supports both WebSocket and HTTP long-polling fallback.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates SocketIO instance with: cors_allowed_origins='*' (allow any origin for dev), async_mode='threading' (use Python threads, not eventlet/gevent), disabled loggers (reduce noise).
entries.perfNotes: Threading mode is simpler but less scalable than eventlet/gevent
entries.securityNotes: cors_allowed_origins='*' should be restricted in production

entries.title: Rate Limiting Configuration
entries.why: Rate limiting prevents API abuse and DoS attacks. The dashboard's polling endpoints need higher limits than typical APIs.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates Flask-Limiter with: key_func=get_remote_address (rate limit by IP), default_limits='1000 per minute' (high for dashboard polling), storage_uri='memory://' (in-memory, not Redis).

failureModes.recovery: No rate limiting, accept the risk or install flask-limiter

entries.perfNotes: In-memory storage loses limits on restart; use Redis for persistence
entries.securityNotes: 1000/min is high - consider lowering for public deployments

entries.title: JSON Error Handlers for API Routes
entries.why: API routes should always return JSON, even on errors. Default Flask error pages return HTML, which breaks JavaScript clients expecting JSON.
entries.whatItDoes: Registers error handlers for 500, 404, 403, 429, 401. Each checks if request.path.startswith('/api/') and returns JSON {'success': False, 'error': '...'} with appropriate status code.
entries.securityNotes: Error messages don't leak stack traces to clients

entries.title: Database Connection Pool
entries.why: Connection pooling is critical for performance. Creating a new database connection per request is expensive (~50ms). Pools reuse connections, reducing latency to ~1ms.
entries.whatItDoes: Creates ThreadedConnectionPool with minconn=5 (always have 5 ready), maxconn=50 (handle concurrent API requests). Logs connection info for debugging. Falls back to direct connections if pool fails.

failureModes.recovery: get_db_connection() falls back to direct psycopg2.connect()
Increase maxconn or optimize query performance

entries.perfNotes: 50 connections can handle ~500 requests/sec with 100ms avg query time

entries.title: Content Security Policy (CSP)
entries.why: CSP headers prevent XSS attacks by controlling which scripts, styles, and connections are allowed. Three.js requires 'unsafe-eval' for shader compilation.
entries.whatItDoes: Configures CSP: script-src allows self + CDNs + unsafe-inline/eval (for Three.js), style-src allows CDNs + Google Fonts, connect-src allows Neon database + CDNs, frame-ancestors='none' (prevent clickjacking).
entries.securityNotes: unsafe-eval is a security tradeoff for Three.js compatibility. Consider using CSP reports to monitor.

entries.title: Machine State Management
entries.why: Tracks which machines (A, B, C) are running and their sensor configurations. This in-memory state is used for real-time display and controls.
entries.whatItDoes: Initializes machine_state dict with rigs A, B, C, each having: running (bool), sensors (dict of sensor_name → {enabled, baseline}). initialize_machine_sensors() populates sensor configs from SENSOR_RANGES.
entries.perfNotes: In-memory state is lost on restart - consider persistence for production

entries.title: Telemetry Cache for 3D Digital Twin
entries.why: The 3D frontend needs current sensor values. Rather than query the database on every request, we cache the latest readings in memory for instant access.
entries.whatItDoes: telemetry_cache: Dict with A/B/C keys, each containing rpm, temperature, vibration, pressure, bearing_temp, anomaly_score. ketchup_telemetry_cache: Dict with L01-L25 keys for 25 production lines.
entries.perfNotes: O(1) access vs O(log N) database query

entries.title: WebSocket Broadcast Workers (10 Hz)
entries.why: The 3D digital twin needs continuous updates at 10 Hz (100ms). Background threads emit cached telemetry to all connected WebSocket clients.
entries.whatItDoes: Infinite loops sleeping 100ms between broadcasts. Each iteration: acquires telemetry_lock, iterates over cache, emits 'rig_telemetry' or 'ketchup_telemetry' event with machine/line data + timestamp.

failureModes.behavior: Logs error, backs off 1 second, continues
failureModes.recovery: Self-healing loop - temporary errors don't crash worker

entries.perfNotes: 10 Hz * 3 rigs = 30 emits/sec; 10 Hz * 25 lines = 250 emits/sec

entries.title: Database Connection Helpers
entries.why: Pool management is error-prone. These helpers abstract getting/returning connections with proper fallbacks and error handling.
entries.whatItDoes: get_db_connection(): Gets connection from pool, falls back to direct connect if pool unavailable. return_db_connection(): Returns connection to pool, closes directly if pool fails.

failureModes.recovery: Callers should check for None and return appropriate error
